examples.en: The camera shook slightly, so the photo is blurry.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 아주 미세한 소리도 잡아내요.
examples.en: This machine picks up even very faint sounds.
The difference between the two products is too subtle.
Just because it's tiny doesn't mean you can ignore it.
The finer it is, the harder it is to check by eye.
The change in taste was so subtle that nobody noticed.

explain: '작다'는 크기가 작을 때 쓰고, '미세하다'는 눈에 거의 안 보이거나 차이가 거의 없을 때 써요. '미세한 차이', '미세하게 떨리다'처럼 뒤에 오는 말을 꾸미는 경우가 많아요. 뉴스에서 자주 듣는 '미세먼지'의 '미세'가 바로 이 말이에요.
explain_en: '작다' is for plain smallness; 미세하다 is for things almost too small to see or differences almost too small to notice. It usually modifies something, as in '미세한 차이' (a subtle difference) or '미세하게 떨리다' (to tremble slightly). The '미세' in the news word 미세먼지 (fine dust) is this word.

examples.ko: 문장 끝에 알맞은 부호를 찍어야 해요.
examples.en: You have to put the right punctuation mark at the end of a sentence.
What does this symbol mean?

examples.ko: 수학 문제에서 부호를 잘못 써서 틀렸어요.
examples.en: I got the math problem wrong because I used the wrong sign.

examples.ko: 친구와 둘만 아는 비밀 부호로 이야기했어요.
examples.en: I talked with my friend in a secret code only the two of us know.
Plus and minus are different signs.

examples.ko: 쉼표 같은 부호는 글을 읽기 쉽게 해 줘요.
examples.en: Marks like commas make writing easier to read.

explain: '기호'와 비슷하지만 '부호'는 문장 부호(. , ? !), 수학의 +와 -, 모스 부호처럼 '정해진 약속의 표시'에 많이 써요. 길거리의 표지나 지도 표시는 보통 '기호'라고 해요. '문장 부호'는 한국어 공부에서 꼭 만나는 말이에요.
explain_en: Close to '기호' (symbol), but 부호 is used for agreed-upon marks such as punctuation (문장 부호), the + and - signs in math, or Morse code. Marks on maps or signs are usually called 기호. 문장 부호 (punctuation) is a term you will meet often in Korean study.

examples.en: That webtoon ended last year.
There is still a long way to go before the story is finished.

examples.ko: 시리즈가 완결돼서 한꺼번에 읽을 수 있어요.
examples.en: The series has ended, so you can read it all at once.
I tend to pick and watch only finished works.

examples.ko: 드라마가 완결되면 팬 모임을 열 거예요.
examples.en: When the drama wraps up, we will hold a fan meeting.
This novel ends in three volumes.

explain: '끝나다'는 아무 일에나 쓰지만 '완결되다'는 소설, 만화, 웹툰, 시리즈처럼 이야기가 끝까지 마무리될 때 주로 써요. 반대말은 '연재되다'(아직 계속 나오는 중)예요. 일을 마친다는 말로는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: '끝나다' works for almost anything, but 완결되다 is mostly used when a story such as a novel, comic, webtoon, or series reaches its proper ending. The opposite is '연재되다' (still being released). It is not used for finishing everyday tasks.

examples.en: The author wrapped up the story, and fans felt sad.

examples.ko: 올해 안에 이 시리즈를 완결할 거예요.
examples.en: I will finish this series within this year.
He finally completed his long serialization.
Bringing a story to its end is harder than I thought.
The trilogy ends with the third book.

examples.ko: 먼저 한 편을 완결하고 다음 작품을 쓸게요.
examples.en: I will finish one piece first and then write the next.

explain: '완결되다'는 이야기가 저절로 끝난 상태를, '완결하다'는 작가나 제작자가 일부러 끝을 내는 행동을 말해요. 대부분 작품에 쓰고 일상적인 일에는 '끝내다', '마치다'를 쓰는 편이에요.
explain_en: 완결되다 describes the state of a story being finished, while 완결하다 is the active version, where the writer or producer brings it to an end. It is mostly for creative works; for everyday tasks Koreans say '끝내다' or '마치다'.

examples.en: Which production company made this movie?
The production company announced a new drama.
My dream is to work at a big production company.
I emailed the game production company with a question.
The production company and the broadcaster signed a contract.

examples.ko: 제작사 이름은 영화가 끝날 때 나와요.
examples.en: The production company's name appears when the movie ends.

explain: 영화·드라마·음악·게임을 실제로 만드는 회사를 말해요. 방송을 내보내는 곳은 '방송사', 물건을 만드는 회사는 보통 '제조사'라고 해서 구별해요.
explain_en: The company that actually makes a film, drama, music, or game. The one that airs it is the '방송사' (broadcaster), and a company that manufactures goods is usually a '제조사'.

examples.en: The paper was withdrawn after the plagiarism came out.
This song was accused of plagiarism.
Schools treat plagiarism very strictly.

examples.ko: 표절 검사를 통과해야 제출할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can submit only after passing the plagiarism check.
Not everything similar is plagiarism.
The director apologized over the plagiarism controversy.

explain: '따라 하다'나 '베끼다'는 일상에서 가볍게 쓰지만 '표절'은 남의 글·노래·그림을 몰래 가져다 자기 것처럼 낸 일을 비판할 때 쓰는 무거운 말이에요. 뉴스와 학교 과제에서 자주 나와요. 법적으로 문제가 될 때는 '저작권 침해'라고 해요.
explain_en: '따라 하다' and '베끼다' can be casual, but 표절 is a serious word for secretly taking someone's writing, music, or art and presenting it as your own. It appears often in the news and in school assignments. When it becomes a legal matter, people say '저작권 침해' (copyright infringement).

examples.en: You must not plagiarize someone else's writing.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 다른 곡을 표절했다는 의심을 받았어요.
examples.en: That singer was suspected of copying another song.

examples.ko: 숙제를 인터넷에서 표절해서 점수를 못 받았어요.
examples.en: I copied my homework from the internet and got no credit.

examples.ko: 표절한 사람은 반드시 책임을 져야 해요.
examples.en: A person who plagiarized must take responsibility.
I did not mean to plagiarize on purpose.
If you do not cite the source, you are plagiarizing.

explain: '베끼다'는 숙제나 시험에도 가볍게 쓰지만, '표절하다'는 글·노래·그림·논문 같은 창작물을 자기 것처럼 내놓았다고 비판할 때 써요. 작품이 주어이면 '표절이다', '표절 의혹이 있다'로 말하는 일이 많아요. 출처를 밝히고 가져오면 '인용하다'예요.
explain_en: '베끼다' can be used lightly, even for homework or tests, but 표절하다 is a criticism for passing off writing, songs, art, or papers as your own. When a work is the subject, people often say '표절이다' or '표절 의혹이 있다'. Taking something while naming the source is '인용하다' (to quote).

examples.ko: 형의 조용한 성격과 동생의 활발한 성격이 대조돼요.
examples.en: The older brother's quiet nature contrasts with the younger's lively one.

examples.ko: 검은 옷이 흰 벽과 대조되어 눈에 띄었어요.
examples.en: The black clothes stood out against the white wall.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 날씨가 크게 대조된다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the weather of the two countries contrasts greatly.
The mood was quiet, in contrast to the flashy stage.
Contrasting with the first part, the story got more fun.

examples.ko: 색이 서로 대조될수록 글씨가 잘 보여요.
examples.en: The more the colors contrast, the easier the text is to read.

explain: 'A와 B가 대조되다'처럼 두 가지가 나란히 있을 때 차이가 뚜렷하게 보인다는 말이에요. 조사는 '-와/과'를 써요. 사람이 비교하는 것은 '대조하다', 저절로 차이가 드러나는 것은 '대조되다'로 구별해요.
explain_en: Used as 'A와 B가 대조되다': when two things sit side by side, the difference between them stands out. The particle is -와/과. A person comparing is 대조하다; differences showing up by themselves is 대조되다.

examples.en: I checked my answer sheet against the correct answers.
They are matching the photo on the ID to the face.
Sign after you check the contract against the original.

examples.ko: 두 문서를 대조하면 다른 부분이 보여요.
examples.en: If you compare the two documents, you can see the differences.

examples.ko: 숫자를 하나씩 대조했지만 틀린 곳이 없었어요.
examples.en: I checked the numbers one by one, but there was no mistake.
I will check the ledger against the receipts.

explain: '비교하다'는 둘의 차이와 같은 점을 보는 것이고, '대조하다'는 하나를 기준으로 삼아 맞는지 확인하는 느낌이 강해요. 서류, 답안, 숫자를 확인할 때 자주 써요. '무엇을 무엇과 대조하다'처럼 '-와/과'가 같이 와요.
explain_en: '비교하다' looks at how two things differ and resemble each other; 대조하다 feels more like checking something against a reference to see whether it matches. It is common with documents, answers, and numbers. It pairs with -와/과: 'A를 B와 대조하다'.

examples.ko: 콘서트 표가 십 분 만에 매진됐어요.
examples.en: The concert tickets sold out in ten minutes.

examples.ko: 인기 있는 빵은 오전에 다 매진돼요.
examples.en: The popular bread sells out completely in the morning.

examples.ko: 영화 표가 매진돼서 다음 시간으로 봤어요.
examples.en: The movie tickets were sold out, so we watched the next showing.

examples.ko: 신제품이 출시 하루 만에 매진되었다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the new product sold out within a day of its release.
Book quickly before it sells out.

examples.ko: 벌써 매진된 공연이라 표를 못 구했어요.
examples.en: It was a show that had already sold out, so I could not get a ticket.

explain: 표나 상품이 모두 팔렸을 때 써요. 가게 앞이나 예매 사이트에서 '매진'이라는 글자를 자주 볼 수 있어요. 물건이 다 떨어졌을 때는 '품절'이라고도 하는데, 공연·영화·기차표에는 '매진', 상품에는 '품절'을 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: Used when tickets or goods have all been sold. You often see '매진' posted at shops and booking sites. '품절' also means out of stock, but 매진 is more common for shows, movies, and train tickets, while 품절 is more common for products.

examples.en: This year I plan to devote myself to studying.

examples.ko: 그는 연구에만 매진해서 좋은 결과를 냈어요.
examples.en: He focused only on research and got good results.

examples.ko: 시험 준비에 매진하느라 친구를 못 만났어요.
examples.en: I couldn't see friends because I was devoted to exam prep.
The athletes are fully committed to Olympic preparation.

examples.ko: 한 가지 일에 매진하면 실력이 늘어요.
examples.en: If you commit to one thing, your skills improve.
Tell me what you were dedicated to.

explain: '매진하다'는 한 가지 일에 온 힘을 쏟는다는 뜻이라 주로 '~에 매진하다'로 써요. '매진되다'(다 팔리다)와 소리는 같지만 뜻이 전혀 달라요. '열중하다'보다 격식 있고 목표를 향해 꾸준히 나아가는 느낌이 있어서 글과 인터뷰에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: Used as '~에 매진하다' (to pour all your effort into something). It sounds just like 매진되다 (sold out) but means something completely different. It is more formal than '열중하다' and carries a sense of steady progress toward a goal, common in writing and interviews.

examples.en: I swear I will never lie again.

examples.ko: 그는 부모님 앞에서 열심히 살겠다고 맹세했어요.
examples.en: He vowed in front of his parents to live diligently.
We swore to stay friends for life.
Can you swear to keep the secret?
My voice trembled a little as I swore.

examples.ko: 결혼식에서 서로 사랑하겠다고 맹세하고 반지를 나눠 꼈어요.
examples.en: At the wedding they vowed to love each other and exchanged rings.

explain: '약속하다'는 가벼운 일에도 쓰지만 '맹세하다'는 목숨이나 명예를 걸 만큼 무겁고 진지한 다짐이에요. '~겠다고 맹세하다' 형태로 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 장난으로 '맹세해!'라고 강조하기도 해요.
explain_en: '약속하다' can be used for small things, but 맹세하다 is a heavy, serious pledge, as if staking your honor on it. It is usually '~겠다고 맹세하다'. In casual talk people also shout '맹세해!' (I swear!) for emphasis.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 조선 시대의 반란을 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class we learned about a rebellion in the Joseon period.
There was news that soldiers had staged a revolt.
In the movie, the robots succeed in their uprising.
The match was turned upside down by a small team's upset.
As the revolt failed, the leader fled.
The staff's revolt started over a pay issue.

explain: '반란'은 나라나 조직 안에서 힘을 가진 쪽에 맞서 일으키는 움직임이에요. 비슷한 '혁명'은 사회를 크게 바꾸는 성공한 변화, '쿠데타'는 군대나 권력자가 갑자기 정권을 빼앗는 일을 말해요. 스포츠에서는 약한 팀이 이길 때 '이변', 가볍게 '반란'이라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 회식이 싫어서 팀원들이 작은 반란을 일으켰어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무력 봉기가 아니라 규칙이나 윗사람에게 가볍게 맞서는 행동을 비유로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Not an armed uprising; a figurative way to describe lightly defying rules or superiors.

explain_en: 반란 is a move to rise against those in power within a country or organization. 혁명 (revolution) means a large, successful change to society, and 쿠데타 (coup) means a sudden seizure of power by the military or leaders. In sports, a weaker team's win is called an '이변' (upset), or jokingly a 반란.

examples.ko: 이 사과는 산지에서 바로 보내 줘요.
examples.en: These apples are sent straight from where they are grown.
Jeju Island is a leading producer of tangerines.
It comes direct from the source, so it is cheap and fresh.

examples.ko: 커피 산지는 대부분 날씨가 따뜻한 곳이에요.
examples.en: Most coffee-growing regions are places with warm weather.
I went to the farm region myself and met the farmers.
Sometimes the place of origin and the producing region differ.

explain: 농산물, 수산물처럼 물건이 만들어지거나 나는 곳이에요. 마트에서 '산지 직송'이라는 광고를 자주 봐요. 소리가 같은 '산지'(산이 많은 땅)도 있지만 이 단어는 '원산지', '주산지'로 연결해서 기억하면 쉬워요.
explain_en: The place where farm or sea products are grown or caught. You often see the ad phrase '산지 직송' (direct from the source) in stores. There is a same-sounding word meaning mountainous land, but this one is easy to remember through '원산지' (country of origin) and '주산지' (main producing area).

examples.ko: 침 속에는 음식을 소화시키는 효소가 있어요.
examples.en: Saliva contains enzymes that digest food.

examples.ko: 요즘 효소 음료가 건강에 좋다고 인기예요.
examples.en: Enzyme drinks are popular these days as good for health.
We learned the role of enzymes in science class.

examples.ko: 파인애플에는 고기를 부드럽게 하는 효소가 들어 있어요.
examples.en: Pineapple has an enzyme that tenderizes meat.

examples.ko: 효소는 온도가 너무 높으면 일을 못 해요.
examples.en: Enzymes cannot work when the temperature is too high.
My grandmother makes plum enzyme syrup by herself.

explain: 과학 시간에 나오는 단어지만 한국에서는 '매실 효소', '곡물 효소'처럼 과일이나 곡물을 설탕에 재워 만든 건강 음료나 식품 이름으로도 자주 써요. 앞에 오는 말과 함께 '소화 효소'처럼 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: A science-class word, but in Korea it is also commonly used for health drinks and foods made by steeping fruit or grain in sugar, as in '매실 효소' (plum enzyme syrup). It often appears in compounds such as '소화 효소' (digestive enzyme).

examples.en: There is a parking lot at the back of the building.
Please sign the back of the card.
The phone's rear camera is better.
The date was written on the back of the photo.
The rear of the car got scratched a bit.
The front and back designs are very different.

explain: 사물의 뒤쪽 면을 말하는 약간 딱딱한 말이에요. 반대말은 '전면'이고, 일상에서는 '뒷면', '뒤쪽'이라고 더 많이 해요. 설명서, 카드, 건물, 카메라처럼 안내문에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: A slightly formal word for the back side of an object. The opposite is '전면' (front), and in daily speech '뒷면' or '뒤쪽' are more common. You see 후면 in manuals, cards, buildings, and camera descriptions.

examples.en: Try listing your favorite foods in order.
The teacher lined up the words on the board.
Just listing the strong points is not persuasive.
Instead of listing reasons, I picked just one.

examples.ko: 할 일을 나열하고 나니 마음이 편해졌어요.
examples.en: After listing what I had to do, I felt more at ease.

examples.ko: 사건을 시간 순서로 나열한 표를 만들었어요.
examples.en: I made a chart listing the events in time order.

explain: '나열하다'는 여러 항목을 차례로 늘어놓듯 말하거나 쓸 때 써요. '열거하다'와 거의 같아요. 물건을 줄 세워 놓을 때는 '늘어놓다', '진열하다'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: 나열하다 is for stating or writing several items one after another. It is almost the same as '열거하다'. For physical objects, '늘어놓다' (spread out) or '진열하다' (display) are more common.

examples.en: I could not find lodging, so I slept outside one night.
It is dangerous to sleep outdoors anywhere other than a campsite.

examples.ko: 여행 중에 공항에서 노숙한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I once slept in an airport while traveling.

examples.ko: 콘서트 표를 사려고 밤새 노숙하는 사람들도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people even sleep outside overnight to buy concert tickets.
It's too cold to sleep outdoors in winter.

examples.ko: 막차를 놓쳐서 역 앞에서 노숙할 뻔했어요.
examples.en: I missed the last train and almost had to sleep outside in front of the station.

explain: 집이나 숙소 없이 밖에서 잠을 잔다는 말이에요. 캠핑처럼 즐기려고 텐트를 치는 것은 '야영하다', 사정이 있어 밖에서 자는 것은 '노숙하다'를 써요. '노숙자'는 집 없이 지내는 사람을 가리켜요.
explain_en: To sleep outside without a house or lodging. For fun, with a tent, it is '야영하다' (to camp); sleeping out because you have no choice is 노숙하다. '노숙자' refers to a person living without a home.

examples.en: My father signed the contract as my agent.

examples.ko: 바쁠 때는 대리인을 보낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: When you are busy, you can send a proxy.
A representative came and picked up the documents on my behalf.
A lawyer is the client's representative.
Try calling the agent directly.

examples.ko: 위임장이 있어야 대리인이 은행 일을 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: An agent can handle bank business only with a letter of authorization.

explain: 다른 사람 대신 일을 처리하는 사람이에요. 은행, 부동산, 법률 일에서 자주 나오고 보통 '위임장'이 필요해요. 회사의 직급 '대리'와 소리가 비슷하지만 다른 단어예요. 가수·배우의 일을 맡은 사람은 '매니저'라고 많이 해요.
explain_en: A person who handles something on someone else's behalf. It comes up with banks, real estate, and legal matters, and usually a '위임장' (letter of authorization) is needed. It sounds like the job title '대리' (assistant manager) but is a different word. A person who handles a singer's or actor's business is commonly called a '매니저'.

examples.en: The squad arrived at the airport yesterday.
The Olympic delegation totals two hundred people.
Fans gave the squad a big round of applause.
The team bus stopped in front of the stadium.
The coach gathered the squad and explained the plan.
Let's sing our team's cheer song together.

explain: 선수들뿐 아니라 감독, 코치, 스태프까지 포함한 팀 전체를 가리킬 때 써요. 선수 개인은 '선수', 한 경기에 나가는 팀은 '팀'이라고 해요. 국가대표나 구단 단위의 큰 무리를 말할 때 자연스러워요.
explain_en: The whole body of a sports team, including players, coaches, and staff. An individual is a '선수' and a team that plays in one game is a '팀'. It sounds natural for national squads or club-level groups.

examples.ko: 많은 분들이 우리 팀을 성원해 주셨어요.
examples.en: Many people cheered on our team.

examples.ko: 끝까지 성원해 주신 팬 여러분께 감사드려요.
examples.en: Thank you to the fans who supported us to the end.
The audience cheering for the athlete was moving.
I will keep supporting you as always.

examples.ko: 응원단이 큰 소리로 성원하자 선수들이 힘을 냈어요.
examples.en: When the cheering squad backed them loudly, the players found new energy.
Citizens eagerly backed the national team.

explain: '응원하다'보다 격식 있고 글이나 인사말에서 많이 써요. 보통 '성원해 주셔서 감사합니다'처럼 도와준 사람에게 고마움을 말할 때 자주 나와요. 가까운 사이의 일상 대화에서는 '응원해'라고 해요.
explain_en: More formal than '응원하다' and common in writing and greetings. You mostly hear it when thanking supporters, as in '성원해 주셔서 감사합니다'. In casual talk between close people, Koreans just say '응원해'.

examples.en: The boss delegated some tasks to the team leader.
We decided to leave the contract matter to the lawyer.
I was busy, so I had a friend handle the paperwork submission.

examples.ko: 권한을 위임하면 일이 더 빨리 끝나요.
examples.en: If you delegate authority, work gets done faster.

examples.ko: 모든 걸 혼자 하지 말고 위임해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't do everything alone; try delegating.

examples.ko: 결정을 위임한 사람이 결과에 책임져야 해요.
examples.en: The person who handed off the decision must answer for the result.

explain: '맡기다'와 비슷하지만 '위임하다'는 일뿐 아니라 그 일을 결정할 권한까지 넘긴다는 느낌이 있어요. 회사, 법률, 행정 이야기에서 주로 나와요. 이때 서류로 만든 증명이 '위임장'이에요. 일상에서 친구에게 부탁할 때는 '맡기다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Like '맡기다' (to leave something to someone), but 위임하다 hands over the authority to decide along with the task. It appears in business, law, and administration, and the written proof is a '위임장'. For asking a friend a favor, '맡기다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: Can I go home now?
Now I get what you mean.
The rain has stopped, so shall we go out now?
Now I can do well even by myself.
I could not see it earlier, but I can see it now.
Stop fighting now and make up.

explain: '이제'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요. 말할 때 편하게 들리고, 글이나 발표에서는 '이제'가 더 일반적이에요.
explain_en: It means the same as '이제' (now). It sounds relaxed in speech, while '이제' is the more general choice in writing and presentations.

examples.en: I had an ultrasound exam at the hospital.
Bats find their way with ultrasonic waves.
Ultrasonic waves cannot be heard by human ears.

examples.ko: 이 세척기는 초음파로 안경을 깨끗이 닦아 줘요.
examples.en: This cleaner washes glasses clean with ultrasound.

examples.ko: 아기의 초음파 사진을 보고 가족이 기뻐했어요.
examples.en: The family was delighted to see the baby's ultrasound picture.
White mist comes out of the ultrasonic humidifier.

explain: 사람이 들을 수 있는 소리보다 높은 소리를 가리켜요. 한국에서는 병원 검사(임신, 복부 초음파)와 가습기·세척기 같은 생활용품 이름에 아주 자주 나와요. 반대로 사람이 들을 수 있는 소리는 '가청음'이라고 해요.
explain_en: Sound waves higher than humans can hear. In Korea it appears very often in hospital exams (pregnancy or abdominal ultrasound) and in household products such as humidifiers and cleaners. Sound within human hearing is called '가청음' (audible sound).

examples.en: When fatigue builds up, the body starts to hurt.
Accumulated experience creates skill.
Building up data takes a long time.

examples.ko: 지방 축적을 막으려면 운동을 해야 해요.
examples.en: To prevent fat build-up, you need to exercise.

examples.ko: 부의 축적 방법을 다룬 책을 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a book about how to accumulate wealth.

examples.ko: 오랜 축적 끝에 이 기술이 나왔어요.
examples.en: This technology came after a long period of accumulation.

explain: 조금씩 쌓여서 많아지는 것을 말하며 '피로 축적', '데이터 축적', '경험 축적'처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것에 자주 써요. 물건을 쌓는 것은 '쌓다'가 자연스러워요. 보통 '축적되다', '축적하다' 형태로 만나요.
explain_en: The gradual piling up of something, mostly intangible things such as fatigue, data, or experience. For physically stacking objects, '쌓다' is more natural. You will most often meet it as 축적되다 or 축적하다.

examples.en: He is a person who has built up knowledge over many years.
The body stores extra energy as fat.
That company has accumulated a lot of data.

examples.ko: 경험을 축적하려면 여러 일을 해 봐야 해요.
examples.en: To build up experience, you have to try many jobs.
Ways of accumulating wealth differ by person.
They built up their technology and are now exporting it.

explain: '모으다'는 동전, 우표, 사람도 모으지만 '축적하다'는 시간을 두고 서서히 쌓아 두는 느낌이 있어서 지식·경험·재산·기술에 어울려요. 형태를 바꿔 '축적되다'라고 하면 저절로 쌓이는 것을 말해요.
explain_en: '모으다' can gather coins, stamps, even people, but 축적하다 suggests slowly storing up over time, so it fits knowledge, experience, wealth, and technology. The passive form 축적되다 describes things that build up by themselves.

examples.en: I explore a new neighborhood every weekend.
The children explored a cave in the forest.
I like movies about exploring space.

examples.ko: 깊은 바다를 탐험하려면 특별한 장비가 필요해요.
examples.en: You need special equipment to explore the deep sea.

examples.ko: 지도 없이 섬을 탐험하다가 길을 잃었어요.
examples.en: I got lost exploring the island without a map.
There are so many places I want to explore.

explain: '여행하다'는 가는 것 자체를, '탐험하다'는 잘 모르는 곳을 위험이나 설렘을 느끼며 알아보러 가는 것을 말해요. 정글, 동굴, 우주처럼 낯선 곳에 잘 어울리고, 가벼운 말로 '동네를 탐험하다'처럼 재미있게도 써요. 명사는 '탐험'이에요.
explain_en: '여행하다' is simply traveling; 탐험하다 is going into an unfamiliar place to find out about it, with a sense of adventure or risk. It suits jungles, caves, and space, and is also used playfully, as in '동네를 탐험하다' (explore the neighborhood). The noun is '탐험'.

examples.en: My bicycle tire went flat.
I was late for school because of a flat tire.

examples.ko: 타이어 펑크는 수리점에서 고칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: A tire puncture can be fixed at a repair shop.
I got a flat on the road and called my insurance company.
If you bail on an appointment, you lose trust.
The show fell through, so I got a refund.

explain: 타이어나 풍선에 구멍이 나서 바람이 빠지는 것이 기본 뜻이에요. 일상에서는 약속이나 일정이 갑자기 빠지거나 취소될 때도 '펑크 나다/내다'라고 말해요. 발음이 같은 음악 장르 '펑크'도 있으니 문맥으로 구별하세요.

phrases.en: to fall through; to have a gap
phrases.nuance_ko: 약속, 일정, 방송처럼 예정된 일이 갑자기 빠지거나 비는 것을 말해요. 돈이 모자랄 때도 '구멍이 났다'는 의미로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a planned appointment, schedule, or broadcast suddenly falls through or has a gap, and sometimes for a shortfall in money.

explain_en: The basic meaning is a hole in a tire or balloon that lets the air out. In daily life it is also used when an appointment or schedule suddenly falls through, as in '펑크 나다/내다'. There is also a same-sounding music genre (punk), so tell them apart by context.

examples.en: My face burned with embarrassment.

examples.ko: 매운 고추를 씹자 입안이 화끈 불붙은 것 같았어요.
examples.en: When I bit into a hot pepper, my mouth felt like it was on fire.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 물이 닿자 손이 화끈 아팠어요.
examples.en: When hot water touched it, my hand stung hotly.
My forehead feels burning hot, maybe from a cold.

examples.ko: 민망한 말을 듣고 귀까지 화끈 뜨거워졌어요.
examples.en: After hearing that embarrassing remark, even my ears flushed hot.
I put a heat pack on in midwinter, and my stomach felt hot.

explain: 몸의 한 곳이 갑자기 뜨거워지는 느낌을 나타내는 의태어예요. 부끄러울 때 '얼굴이 화끈거리다', 매운 걸 먹은 뒤 '입이 화끈거리다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 '후끈'은 공기나 방이 갑자기 더워지는 느낌에 더 어울려요.
explain_en: An onomatopoeic adverb for a part of the body suddenly feeling hot. Used as '얼굴이 화끈거리다' when embarrassed or '입이 화끈거리다' after eating spicy food. The similar '후끈' fits air or a room suddenly turning warm.

en: burning hot; flushed; bold and generous

examples.en: The stew was so fiery that I started sweating.
He is a person with a bold, straightforward personality.
The boss treated everyone generously.
The action is intense, so give it a watch.
I tried a spicy fish stew place that is known to be fiery.

examples.ko: 한 번 하려면 화끈하게 해야 해요.
examples.en: If you're going to do it, you have to go all out.

explain: 몸이나 음식이 뜨겁고 매울 때도 쓰지만, 사람에게 쓰면 망설이지 않고 시원시원하게 행동하는 성격을 칭찬하는 말이에요. '화끈하게 쏘다(크게 한턱내다)', '화끈한 액션'처럼 말해요. 비슷한 '시원시원하다'는 좀 더 부드러운 느낌이에요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 한턱을 크게 낸다는 관용적 표현이에요. 뜨겁다는 원래 뜻만으로는 짐작하기 어려워요.
phrases.nuance_en: An idiomatic phrase for picking up the bill in a big way; you cannot guess it from the literal 'hot' meaning.
phrases.en_equiv: treat everyone; pick up the tab in style

explain_en: It can describe something hot or spicy, but said of a person it praises a bold, no-hesitation personality. Examples: '화끈하게 쏘다' (treat everyone generously) or '화끈한 액션' (a gutsy action scene). The similar '시원시원하다' sounds a bit gentler.

en: photo spread; pictorial; collection of pictures

examples.en: That actor did a magazine photo shoot.
The new album's photo set was released today.
I made plans while looking at a travel photo book.

examples.ko: 화보 촬영 때문에 일찍 일어나야 해요.
examples.en: I have to get up early for the photo shoot.
I booked a session to shoot wedding photos.

examples.ko: 화보 속 모습이 실제와 달라서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised that the person in the photo spread looks different in real life.

explain: 잡지나 책에서 사진을 중심으로 꾸민 쪽이나 사진 모음을 가리켜요. 연예인 이야기에서 '화보 촬영', '화보 공개'가 정말 자주 나와요. 일반 '사진'보다 콘셉트와 연출이 있는 사진 작업이라는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: Pages or a collection built around photographs in a magazine or book. In celebrity news, '화보 촬영' (photo shoot) and '화보 공개' (photo set release) appear constantly. Compared with a plain '사진', it suggests a styled, concept-driven photo project.

examples.en: There is a camera at the back of the car.
Reverse parking is still hard for me.
The defenders pass the ball slowly at the back.
The ball rolled back and a defender caught it.

examples.ko: 후방이 안전해야 앞에서 마음 놓고 일할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only when the back is safe can people work freely at the front.
The rear sensor beeped, so I stopped the car.

explain: 사물이나 대열의 뒤쪽을 말하는 격식 있는 말이에요. 군대에서는 전선 뒤쪽을 '후방', 앞쪽을 '전방'이라고 해요. 운전할 때는 '후방 카메라', '후방 주차', '후방 감지기'로 자주 만나요. 일상에서 그냥 뒤를 말할 때는 '뒤', '뒤쪽'이 훨씬 자연스러워요.
explain_en: A formal word for the back of an object or formation. In the military, the area behind the front line is '후방' and the front is '전방'. In driving you meet it in '후방 카메라', '후방 주차', and '후방 감지기'. In everyday speech '뒤' or '뒤쪽' sounds much more natural.

examples.en: When the power went out, we turned on the generator.
At the campsite they use a small generator.
The hospital has an emergency generator.
The generator is too noisy.
The wind turbine generator is spinning in the wind.
At the construction site they make electricity with a generator.

explain: 전기를 만들어 내는 기계예요. '발전소'는 전기를 만드는 큰 시설, '발전기'는 그 안이나 캠핑·공사장에서 쓰는 기계라는 점이 달라요. 소리가 같은 '발전기(發展期)'는 발전해 가는 시기를 뜻하니 문맥으로 구별하세요.
explain_en: A machine that produces electricity. A '발전소' is a large power plant, while a 발전기 is the machine inside it or one used at campsites and construction sites. There is also a same-sounding 발전기 (發展期) meaning a period of development, so tell them apart by context.

examples.en: I hope everyone stays healthy.
He always wished for his family to be happy.
I wrote a piece wishing for peace in the new year.
The thing I had hoped for finally came true.
We said goodbye wishing each other success.
If you wish earnestly, a way will open.

explain: '바라다'와 뜻은 가깝지만 '소망하다'는 더 간절하고 진지한 느낌이라 인사말, 편지, 기도, 글에서 자주 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '바라요', '빌어요'가 더 자연스러워요. 같은 뜻의 명사는 '소망'이고 '소원'과 거의 비슷하게 써요.
explain_en: Close to '바라다' (to hope), but 소망하다 feels more earnest and serious, so it appears in greetings, letters, prayers, and writing. In daily talk, '바라요' or '빌어요' sound more natural. The noun '소망' is used almost like '소원' (a wish).
